title: OES-512 Telemetry Engine: synthetic 512-channel framing, filtering and summary statistics
description:
A small asynchronous Python prototype that frames, filters and summarizes synthetic 512-channel telemetry: binary frames with a header, sequence ID, timestamp and checksum; a stateful 50 Hz notch and 0.5-45 Hz Butterworth bandpass per channel; and rolling-window statistics.

The statistics are plain definitions: 'coherence' is the mean absolute Pearson correlation over 32 sampled channels, 'instability' is the standard deviation of per-channel variances, and 'drift' is the distance of the per-channel mean from the first full window. Threshold alerts go to a local log; webhook POSTs are opt-in.

Scope: all input comes from a deterministic built-in generator with a synthetic step disturbance. It is not acquisition hardware, has no connection to real sensors, and no latency or throughput has been measured; alert thresholds are uncalibrated defaults.

Python 3.10+, NumPy and SciPy. 11 pytest tests and an end-to-end demo run in GitHub Actions. License: AGPL-3.0-only (commercial licence available).
